--- Transcript (timestamps approximate, transcription imperfect) ---
[00:00] Sam Chen: Hey everyone, welcome, thanks for joining — really excited to have BrightWave here, Jenna, Liam, thanks for taking time. This is more of a podcast style conversation so we'll keep it casual.
[00:12] Jenna Morales: Yeah thanks, happy to be here. Um, excited to talk about the work we've done with Redwood.
[00:18] Liam O'Connor: Thanks Sam. Hi Alex, Priya, yeah hi all.
[00:22] Alex Gomez: great to see you. Um I'll just do a quick intro, I'm Alex on the sales side but been working with BrightWave on the contract and ensuring the DL's, um, throughput commitments.
[00:31] Priya Nair: And I'm Priya from the SE team, I worked on the benchmarks and the migration plan.
[00:36] Jenna Morales: Cool. Um, maybe Liam you can start — like how did BrightWave come to decide to use Redwood?
[00:43] Liam O'Connor: Sure. So, we had been running a hybrid approach before — some queries on OpenAI hosted endpoints, some on our in-house Triton clusters. The problem was, as we ship more realtime analytics in product, latency spiked and cost became unpredictable. We needed something that could give consistent p95 latency and also be flexible between hosted and private, because we have regulated customers that insist on data residency.
[01:07] Jenna Morales: Yeah we were also looking at Anthropic for a bit but the economics weren't as attractive for the scale we do.
[01:13] Sam Chen: When did you first try Redwood? Was there a POC?
[01:16] Liam O'Connor: We kicked off a two-week POC in July. Alex and Priya helped set up a dedicated pool for our main model family, and we ran one of our common query workloads through it — real user traffic replay, session-based queries.
[01:29] Priya Nair: I remember the replay, there was some headroom on KV cache effectiveness which helped, you know, reduce repeated prefix compute. We also tried the quantized variant for some of the embeddings.
[01:39] Liam O'Connor: Right and that cache saved us a ton; for our churn predictions and on-page suggestions it cut token cost per request by almost 35% in the POC.
[01:47] Alex Gomez: And on latency? I recall the p95 numbers improved.
[01:50] Priya Nair: We saw p50 around 80ms and p95 around 220ms for the main 512-token flows on a dedicated rtx-like pool, compared to 300-450ms before on the self-hosted cluster during peak. Those numbers are in the benchmark sheet.
[02:06] Jenna Morales: That's huge. From the growth side, we saw conversion on the interactive onboarding flow increase by a couple points after we made the swap. So it's not just infra wins, it's product impact.
[02:16] Liam O'Connor: There's also the observability — Redwood Console's dashboards made it way easier for our platform team to attribute cost back to features. Before, it was pretty opaque.
[02:26] Sam Chen: I know you had some strict security asks early on — VPC peering, KMS integration, SOC 2. How did that process go?
[02:33] Liam O'Connor: It was pretty smooth. We did the private deployment for our EU customers, and Redwood's compliance pack plus the KMS integration ticked the boxes. There was one audit question about retention settings and logs, but Alex got the security docs and the SOC 2 report over quickly.
[02:47] Alex Gomez: Yep we shared the SOC 2, ISO notes, and the audit log export process.
[02:51] Jenna Morales: There was a small hiccup with an SSO mapping but Priya helped debug the SAML assertions.
[02:57] Priya Nair: Right, that was more of an IdP config on BrightWave's side — fixed in the staging SAML metadata exchange.
[03:04] Liam O'Connor: One of the things that surprised us was the ability to route by policy. We route lower-sensitivity traffic to the hosted cluster to save cost, and high-sensitivity traffic to our private cluster. Redwood's fallback policies also meant that if a region had pressure, requests would failover gracefully.
[03:20] Sam Chen: That's a pattern we've seen with other enterprise customers too — the hybrid routing saves a lot of $$.
[03:25] Jenna Morales: On the marketing front, the reduction in latency made the demo videos much smoother, we captured that in our webinar and saw a lift. We're planning a joint webinar actually.
[03:35] Alex Gomez: Awesome. Any feedback about the onboarding or docs?
[03:39] Liam O'Connor: The docs were fine, but the step-by-step for the private deployment could be clearer — mostly network diagram examples. Priya — that was your doc?
[03:47] Priya Nair: Yeah we actually have an internal playbook; I'll share an abridged network diagram and the checklist.
[03:52] Jenna Morales: For the case study, we want a bit of narrative — timeline, the p95 and cost delta, and a short quote from Liam. We'll also need logo usage and the legal release.
[04:01] Sam Chen: Sure, Sam (that's me) will draft and circulate. We'll get a pull quote from Liam and a short blurb from Jenna on growth impact.
[04:08] Liam O'Connor: Happy to provide a quote. Um, just flag — legal wants to review the wording; we'll need a quick approval loop.
[04:15] Sam Chen: Totally, we'll send the draft with a redline-ready section for legal.
[04:18] Jenna Morales: Also, Priya, can you give us the raw CSV of the test runs and the config of the rtx nodes? Marketing would like a graph for the case study.
[04:26] Priya Nair: Yep I'll export the CSV and include the instance types, quantization flags, and batching config. the sheet link should have everything by end of week.
[04:34] Alex Gomez: Are there any remaining blockers from BrightWave's side to publish the case study?
[04:38] Liam O'Connor: Just the legal approval and a quick marketing review. Otherwise we're green.
[04:43] Jenna Morales: We'll aim to return approval within three business days of receiving the draft.
[04:48] Sam Chen: Great. Quick note for listeners — BrightWave used the Redwood Dedicated plan for their EU private cluster and kept some traffic on hosted to optimize cost.
[04:58] Liam O'Connor: One small technical note — we used prefix KV caching aggressively for our conversational history, that cut token recompute and improved cost. Also, the runtime's kernel selection meant the inference on longer sequences didn't blow up latency like our previous setup.
[05:14] Priya Nair: We also tested a 4-bit quantized variant for internal embeddings which saved memory and allowed higher throughput during peak, with minimal quality impact on our reranker.
[05:24] Jenna Morales: From the measurement side we match key success metrics: p95 latency requirement 250ms met, and 30% cost reduction vs prior infra.
[05:33] Sam Chen: That's a nice headline. Anything else you want included in the case study?
[05:37] Liam O'Connor: Maybe a short section on governance — how we use RBAC and audit logs to meet compliance. That helps other regulated customers relate.
[05:45] Sam Chen: Good call. We'll include a governance sidebar.
[05:48] Jenna Morales: And a short quote on product impact — conversion lift stats.
[05:52] Sam Chen: We'll draft those.
[05:54] Alex Gomez: For the podcast clip marketing wants a 60-second soundbite — we can pull the section where Liam talks about the p95 and conversion lift.
[06:02] Jenna Morales: Perfect.
[06:04] Sam Chen: Ok, recap quick: Sam will draft case study and send to Liam by Dec 22; Priya will export benchmark CSV and network diagram by Dec 18; Jenna provide quote/logo by Dec 19; marketing will produce clip. Any objections?
[06:18] Liam O'Connor: No objections, sounds good.
[06:20] Jenna Morales: Yep good.
[06:22] Sam Chen: Cool, thanks so much everyone. We'll follow up in email.
[06:25] [crosstalk] 
[06:30] End of recording.
